audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for journey to Jerusalem, daughters prophesying, Agabus binding sign, James/elders, purification, temple arrest, Roman rescue, Hebrew address setup.

verses.restored: When we had torn ourselves away from them and put out to sea, running straight we came to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:

modern.text: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

original.text: Ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ἀναχθῆναι ἡμᾶς ἀποσπασθέντας ἀπʼ αὐτῶν, εὐθυδρομήσαντες ἤλθομεν εἰς τὴν ⸀Κῶ, τῇ δὲ ἑξῆς εἰς τὴν Ῥόδον, κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Πάταρα·

verses.restored: Finding a ship crossing to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.

familiar.text: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.

modern.text: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.

original.text: καὶ εὑρόντες πλοῖον διαπερῶν εἰς Φοινίκην ἐπιβάντες ἀνήχθημεν.

verses.restored: Coming in sight of Cyprus and leaving it on the left, we sailed to Syria and came down to Tyre, for there the ship was unloading cargo.

familiar.text: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.

modern.text: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.

original.text: ⸀ἀναφάναντες δὲ τὴν Κύπρον καὶ καταλιπόντες αὐτὴν εὐώνυμον ἐπλέομεν εἰς Συρίαν, καὶ ⸀κατήλθομεν εἰς Τύρον, ἐκεῖσε γὰρ ⸂τὸ πλοῖον ἦν⸃ ἀποφορτιζόμενον τὸν γόμον.

verses.restored: Finding the disciples, we remained there seven days. Through the Spirit they were saying to Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

modern.text: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

original.text: ⸂ἀνευρόντες δὲ τοὺς⸃ μαθητὰς ἐπεμείναμεν αὐτοῦ ἡμέρας ἑπτά, οἵτινες τῷ Παύλῳ ἔλεγον διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος μὴ ⸀ἐπιβαίνειν εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα.

verses.restored: When our days were completed, we departed and went on, all of them with wives and children accompanying us until outside the city. Kneeling on the shore, we prayed.

familiar.text: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.

modern.text: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.

original.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ⸂ἐξαρτίσαι ἡμᾶς⸃ τὰς ἡμέρας, ἐξελθόντες ἐπορευόμεθα προπεμπόντων ἡμᾶς πάντων σὺν γυναιξὶ καὶ τέκνοις ἕως ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, καὶ θέντες τὰ γόνατα ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν ⸀προσευξάμενοι

verses.restored: Having said farewell to one another, we went up into the ship, and they returned to their own.

familiar.text: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.

modern.text: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.

original.text: ⸂ἀπησπασάμεθα ἀλλήλους, καὶ⸃ ⸀ἐνέβημεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὰ ἴδια.

verses.restored: Completing the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais, greeted the siblings, and remained one day with them.

familiar.text: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.

modern.text: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day. Paul Visits Philip the Evangelist

original.text: Ἡμεῖς δὲ τὸν πλοῦν διανύσαντες ἀπὸ Τύρου κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Πτολεμαΐδα, καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἐμείναμεν ἡμέραν μίαν παρʼ αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: On the next day, departing, we came to Caesarea and entered the house of Philip the good-news announcer, who was one of the seven, and remained with him.

familiar.text: And the next day we that were of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.

modern.text: Leaving the next day, we went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the Seven.

original.text: τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντες ⸀ἤλθομεν εἰς Καισάρειαν, καὶ εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον Φιλίππου τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ ὄντος ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐμείναμεν παρʼ αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: This one had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.

familiar.text: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.

modern.text: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.

original.text: τούτῳ δὲ ἦσαν θυγατέρες ⸂τέσσαρες παρθένοι⸃ προφητεύουσαι.

verses.restored: As we remained many days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

familiar.text: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.

modern.text: After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

original.text: ἐπιμενόντων ⸀δὲ ἡμέρας πλείους κατῆλθέν τις ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας προφήτης ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος,

verses.restored: Coming to us and taking Paul's belt, he bound his own feet and hands and said, Thus says the holy Spirit: The man whose belt this is, the Judeans in Jerusalem will bind in this way and hand over into the hands of nations.

familiar.text: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.

modern.text: Coming over to us, he took Paul’s belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.’”

original.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἄρας τὴν ζώνην τοῦ Παύλου δήσας ⸀ἑαυτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν· Τάδε λέγει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον Τὸν ἄνδρα οὗ ἐστιν ἡ ζώνη αὕτη, οὕτως δήσουσιν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ παραδώσουσιν εἰς χεῖρας ἐθνῶν.

verses.restored: When we heard these things, both we and those local were urging him not to go up to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.

modern.text: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἠκούσαμεν ταῦτα, παρεκαλοῦμεν ἡμεῖς τε καὶ οἱ ἐντόπιοι τοῦ μὴ ἀναβαίνειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.

verses.restored: Then Paul answered, What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

familiar.text: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

modern.text: Then Paul answered, “Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

original.text: ⸂τότε ἀπεκρίθη⸃ ὁ Παῦλος· Τί ποιεῖτε κλαίοντες καὶ συνθρύπτοντές μου τὴν καρδίαν; ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐ μόνον δεθῆναι ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀποθανεῖν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἑτοίμως ἔχω ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: Since he was not persuaded, we became quiet, saying, Let the will of the Lord happen.

familiar.text: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.

modern.text: When he would not be dissuaded, we fell silent and said, “The Lord’s will be done.”

original.text: μὴ πειθομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἡσυχάσαμεν εἰπόντες· ⸂Τοῦ κυρίου τὸ θέλημα⸃ ⸀γινέσθω.

verses.restored: After these days, preparing, we went up to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.

modern.text: After these days, we packed up and went on to Jerusalem.

original.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ταύτας ἐπισκευασάμενοι ἀνεβαίνομεν εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα·

verses.restored: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also came with us, bringing us to Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would lodge.

familiar.text: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.

modern.text: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple. Paul’s Arrival at Jerusalem

original.text: συνῆλθον δὲ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν ἀπὸ Καισαρείας σὺν ἡμῖν, ἄγοντες παρʼ ᾧ ξενισθῶμεν Μνάσωνί τινι Κυπρίῳ, ἀρχαίῳ μαθητῇ.

verses.restored: When we came to Jerusalem, the siblings received us gladly.

familiar.text: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.

modern.text: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us joyfully.

original.text: Γενομένων δὲ ἡμῶν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀσμένως ⸀ἀπεδέξαντο ἡμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοί.

verses.restored: On the next day Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders were present.

familiar.text: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.

modern.text: The next day Paul went in with us to see James, and all the elders were present.

original.text: τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰσῄει ὁ Παῦλος σὺν ἡμῖν πρὸς Ἰάκωβον, πάντες τε παρεγένοντο οἱ πρεσβύτεροι.

verses.restored: Greeting them, he described one by one the things the Divine had done among the nations through his service.

familiar.text: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.

modern.text: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.

original.text: καὶ ἀσπασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐξηγεῖτο καθʼ ἓν ἕκαστον ὧν ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν διὰ τῆς διακονίας αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Hearing, they glorified the Divine and said to him, You see, sibling, how many myriads there are among the Judeans who have trusted, and all are zealous for the Law.

familiar.text: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:

modern.text: When they heard this, they glorified God. Then they said to Paul, “You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν ⸀θεόν, ⸂εἶπόν τε⸃ αὐτῷ· Θεωρεῖς, ἀδελφέ, πόσαι μυριάδες εἰσὶν ⸂ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις⸃ τῶν πεπιστευκότων, καὶ πάντες ζηλωταὶ τοῦ νόμου ὑπάρχουσιν·

verses.restored: They have been informed about you that you teach all the Judeans among the nations apostasy from Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or walk in the customs.

familiar.text: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.

modern.text: But they are under the impression that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or observe our customs.

original.text: κατηχήθησαν δὲ περὶ σοῦ ὅτι ἀποστασίαν διδάσκεις ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως τοὺς κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη πάντας Ἰουδαίους, λέγων μὴ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς τὰ τέκνα μηδὲ τοῖς ἔθεσιν περιπατεῖν.

verses.restored: What then is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come.

familiar.text: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.

modern.text: What then should we do? They will certainly hear that you have come.

original.text: τί οὖν ἐστιν; πάντως ⸀ἀκούσονται ὅτι ἐλήλυθας.

verses.restored: Therefore do this that we say to you: there are four men with us having a vow upon themselves.

familiar.text: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;

modern.text: Therefore do what we advise you. There are four men with us who have taken a vow.

original.text: τοῦτο οὖν ποίησον ὅ σοι λέγομεν· εἰσὶν ἡμῖν ἄνδρες τέσσαρες εὐχὴν ἔχοντες ⸀ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν.

verses.restored: Take these and purify yourself with them, and pay expenses for them, so that they may shave the head, and all will know there is nothing to the things they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk guarding the Law.

familiar.text: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.

modern.text: Take these men, purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses so they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you, but that you also live in obedience to the law.

original.text: τούτους παραλαβὼν ἁγνίσθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς καὶ δαπάνησον ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς ἵνα ⸀ξυρήσονται τὴν κεφαλήν, καὶ ⸀γνώσονται πάντες ὅτι ὧν κατήχηνται περὶ σοῦ οὐδέν ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ στοιχεῖς καὶ αὐτὸς ⸂φυλάσσων τὸν νόμον⸃.

verses.restored: But concerning those from the nations who have trusted, we wrote, judging that they should guard themselves from idol-offering, blood, strangled things, and sexual immorality.

familiar.text: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.

modern.text: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.”

original.text: περὶ δὲ τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἐθνῶν ἡμεῖς ⸀ἀπεστείλαμεν ⸀κρίναντες φυλάσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς τό τε εἰδωλόθυτον ⸀καὶ αἷμα καὶ πνικτὸν καὶ πορνείαν.

verses.restored: Then Paul took the men, and the next day, being purified with them, entered the temple, announcing the completion of the days of purification until the offering was offered for each one of them.

familiar.text: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.

modern.text: So the next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he entered the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete and the offering would be made for each of them. Paul Seized at the Temple

original.text: τότε ὁ Παῦλος παραλαβὼν τοὺς ἄνδρας τῇ ἐχομένῃ ἡμέρᾳ σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁγνισθεὶς εἰσῄει εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, διαγγέλλων τὴν ἐκπλήρωσιν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ ἁγνισμοῦ ἕως οὗ προσηνέχθη ὑπὲρ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου αὐτῶν ἡ προσφορά.

verses.restored: When the seven days were about to be completed, the Judeans from Asia, seeing him in the temple, stirred up all the crowd and laid hands on him,

familiar.text: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,

modern.text: When the seven days were almost over, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,

original.text: Ὡς δὲ ἔμελλον αἱ ἑπτὰ ἡμέραι συντελεῖσθαι, οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι θεασάμενοι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ συνέχεον πάντα τὸν ὄχλον καὶ ἐπέβαλον ⸂ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας⸃,

verses.restored: crying out, Men of Israel, help. This is the human teaching everyone everywhere against the people, the Law, and this place. And besides, he also brought Greeks into the temple and has made this holy place common.

familiar.text: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.

modern.text: crying out, “Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who teaches everywhere against our people and against our law and against this place. Furthermore, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”

original.text: κράζοντες· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, βοηθεῖτε· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ κατὰ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τοῦ τόπου τούτου πάντας ⸀πανταχῇ διδάσκων, ἔτι τε καὶ Ἕλληνας εἰσήγαγεν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ κεκοίνωκεν τὸν ἅγιον τόπον τοῦτον.

verses.restored: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, whom they supposed Paul had brought into the temple.

familiar.text: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

modern.text: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

original.text: ἦσαν γὰρ ⸀προεωρακότες Τρόφιμον τὸν Ἐφέσιον ἐν τῇ πόλει σὺν αὐτῷ, ὃν ἐνόμιζον ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν εἰσήγαγεν ὁ Παῦλος.

verses.restored: The whole city was moved, and there was a running together of the people. Taking hold of Paul, they were dragging him outside the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.

familiar.text: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.

modern.text: The whole city was stirred up, and the people rushed together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the gates were shut.

original.text: ἐκινήθη τε ἡ πόλις ὅλη καὶ ἐγένετο συνδρομὴ τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενοι τοῦ Παύλου εἷλκον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ εὐθέως ἐκλείσθησαν αἱ θύραι.

verses.restored: As they were seeking to kill him, a report went up to the commander of the cohort that all Jerusalem was in confusion.

familiar.text: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

modern.text: While they were trying to kill him, the commander of the Roman regiment received a report that all Jerusalem was in turmoil.

original.text: ζητούντων ⸀τε αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἀνέβη φάσις τῷ χιλιάρχῳ τῆς σπείρης ὅτι ὅλη ⸀συγχύννεται Ἰερουσαλήμ,

verses.restored: At once taking soldiers and centurions, he ran down upon them. Seeing the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

familiar.text: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.

modern.text: Immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

original.text: ὃς ἐξαυτῆς παραλαβὼν στρατιώτας καὶ ἑκατοντάρχας κατέδραμεν ἐπʼ αὐτούς, οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ τοὺς στρατιώτας ἐπαύσαντο τύπτοντες τὸν Παῦλον.

verses.restored: Then the commander, coming near, seized him and commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he might be and what he had done.

familiar.text: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.

modern.text: The commander came up and arrested Paul, ordering that he be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.

original.text: ⸂τότε ἐγγίσας⸃ ὁ χιλίαρχος ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκέλευσε δεθῆναι ἁλύσεσι δυσί, καὶ ἐπυνθάνετο ⸀τίς εἴη καὶ τί ἐστιν πεποιηκώς.

verses.restored: Some in the crowd were shouting one thing, some another. Not being able to know the certainty because of the uproar, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.

familiar.text: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.

modern.text: Some in the crowd were shouting one thing, and some another. And since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks.

original.text: ἄλλοι δὲ ἄλλο τι ⸀ἐπεφώνουν ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ· μὴ ⸂δυναμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ⸃ γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς διὰ τὸν θόρυβον ἐκέλευσεν ἄγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν.

verses.restored: When he came upon the stairs, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd.

familiar.text: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.

modern.text: When Paul reached the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob.

original.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀναβαθμούς, συνέβη βαστάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν διὰ τὴν βίαν τοῦ ὄχλου,

verses.restored: For the multitude of the people followed, crying out, Take him away.

familiar.text: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.

modern.text: For the crowd that followed him kept shouting, “Away with him!” Paul Addresses the Crowd

original.text: ἠκολούθει γὰρ τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ ⸀κράζοντες· Αἶρε αὐτόν.

verses.restored: As he was about to be brought into the barracks, Paul says to the commander, Is it permitted for me to say something to you? He said, Do you know Greek?

familiar.text: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?

modern.text: As they were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, “May I say something to you?” “Do you speak Greek?” he replied.

original.text: Μέλλων τε εἰσάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ὁ Παῦλος λέγει τῷ χιλιάρχῳ· Εἰ ἔξεστίν μοι εἰπεῖν ⸀τι πρὸς σέ; ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἑλληνιστὶ γινώσκεις;

verses.restored: Then you are not the Egyptian who before these days stirred up and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?

familiar.text: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?

modern.text: “Aren’t you the Egyptian who incited a rebellion some time ago and led four thousand members of the ‘Assassins’ into the wilderness?”

original.text: οὐκ ἄρα σὺ εἶ ὁ Αἰγύπτιος ὁ πρὸ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀναστατώσας καὶ ἐξαγαγὼν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους ἄνδρας τῶν σικαρίων;

verses.restored: Paul said, I am a Judean man from Tarsus of Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I ask you, permit me to speak to the people.

familiar.text: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.

modern.text: But Paul answered, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Now I beg you to allow me to speak to the people.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος· Ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος μέν εἰμι Ἰουδαῖος, Ταρσεὺς τῆς Κιλικίας, οὐκ ἀσήμου πόλεως πολίτης· δέομαι δέ σου, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι λαλῆσαι πρὸς τὸν λαόν.

verses.restored: When he permitted him, Paul, standing on the stairs, motioned with the hand to the people. When there was great silence, he addressed them in the Hebrew dialect, saying:

familiar.text: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,

modern.text: Having received permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. A great hush came over the crowd, and he addressed them in Hebrew:

original.text: ἐπιτρέψαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος ἑστὼς ἐπὶ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν κατέσεισε τῇ χειρὶ τῷ λαῷ, πολλῆς δὲ σιγῆς γενομένης ⸀προσεφώνησεν τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ λέγων
